question.text: What is the quotient of $x^3 + 2x^2 + x + 1$ divided by $x^2+2x+1?$
question.explanation:
Using the method of polynomial division, we obtain the following:

\begin{align*} \require{enclose} & \phantom{x^2+2x+2} \:\:\:\:\: {\color{blue}x} \\ & {x^2+2x+1} \: \enclose{longdiv}{\:\, x^3+2x^2+x+1 \:\:} \\ & \phantom{x^2+2x+2} \:\:\:\:\: \underline{x^3+2x^2+x} \\ & \phantom{x^2+2x+2} \:\:\:\:\: \phantom{x^3+2x^2+x+} \: 1 \end{align*}

Therefore,

  • the quotient is ${\color{blue}x},$ and

  • the remainder is ${1}.$

question.text: What is the quotient of $48x^3 + 16x^2 - 12x - 4$ divided by $12x^2-2x-2?$
question.explanation:
Using the method of polynomial division, we obtain the following:

\begin{align*} \require{enclose} & \phantom{12x^2-2x-2} \:\:\:\:\: {\color{blue}4x+2} \\ & {12x^2-2x-2} \: \enclose{longdiv}{\:\, 48x^3+16x^2-12x-4 \:\:} \\ & \phantom{12x^2-2x-2} \:\:\:\:\: \underline{48x^3-\phantom{0}8x^2-\phantom{0}8x} \\ & \phantom{12x^2-2x-2} \:\:\:\:\: \phantom{48x^3+} \:\: 24x^2-\phantom{0}4x-4 \\ & \phantom{12x^2-2x-2} \:\:\:\:\:\: \phantom{48x^3+} \: \underline{24x^2-\phantom{0}4x-4} \\ & \phantom{12x^2-2x-2} \:\:\:\:\:\: \phantom{48x^3 +24x^2-4x+} \:\:\: {0} \end{align*}

Therefore,

  • the quotient is ${\color{blue}4x+2},$ and

  • the remainder is ${0}.$

question.text: What is the remainder when $3x^3-2x^2-18x-1$ is divided by $3x^2-8x-2?$
question.explanation:
Using the method of polynomial division, we obtain the following:

\begin{align*} \require{enclose} & \phantom{3x^2-8x-2} \:\:\:\:\: {x+2} \\ & {3x^2-8x-2} \: \enclose{longdiv}{\:\, 3x^3-2x^2-18x-1 \:\:} \\ & \phantom{3x^2-8x-2} \:\:\:\:\: \underline{3x^3-8x^2-\phantom{0}2x} \\ & \phantom{3x^2-8x-2} \:\:\:\:\: \phantom{3x^3+} \:\: 6x^2-16x-1 \\ & \phantom{3x^2-8x-2} \:\:\:\:\:\: \phantom{3x^3+} \: \underline{6x^2-16x-4} \\ & \phantom{3x^2-8x-2} \:\:\:\:\:\: \phantom{3x^3+6x^2-16x+} \: {\color{blue}3} \end{align*}

Therefore,

  • the quotient is $x+2,$ and

  • the remainder is ${\color{blue}3}.$

question.text: What is the quotient of $3x^3 - 2x^2 - x - 1$ divided by $x^2+x+1?$
question.explanation:
Using the method of polynomial division, we obtain the following:

\begin{align*} \require{enclose} & \phantom{x^2+x+1} \:\:\:\:\: {\color{blue}3x- 5} \\ & {x^2+x+1} \: \enclose{longdiv}{\:\, 3x^3-2x^2-\phantom{0}x-1 \:\:} \\ & \phantom{x^2+x+1} \:\:\:\:\: \underline{3x^3+3x^2+3x} \\ & \phantom{x^2+x+1} \:\:\:\:\: \phantom{3x^3} -5x^2-4x-1 \\ & \phantom{x^2+x+1} \:\:\:\:\:\: \phantom{3x^3} \underline{-\,5x^2-5x-5} \\ & \phantom{x^2+x+1} \:\:\:\:\:\: \phantom{3x^3 -5x^2-4} \! {x+4} \end{align*}

Therefore,

  • the quotient is ${\color{blue}3x-5},$ and

  • the remainder is ${x+4}.$

exampleAnswers.title: Dividing a Quartic Polynomial by a Quadratic or Cubic Polynomial

question.explanation:
Using the method of polynomial division, we obtain the following:

\begin{align*} \require{enclose} & \phantom{2x^2 - x - 2} \:\:\:\:\: 2x^2 - 2 \\ & 2x^2 - x - 2 \: \enclose{longdiv}{\:\, 4x^4-2x^3-8x^2+3x+1 \:\:} \\ & \phantom{2x^2 - x - 2} \:\:\:\:\: \underline{4x^4-2x^3-4x^2} \\ & \phantom{2x^2 - x - 2} \:\:\:\:\: \phantom{4x^4-2x^3} -4x^2+3x+1 \\ & \phantom{2x^2 - x - 2} \:\:\:\:\:\: \phantom{4x^4-2x^3} \underline{-\,4x^2+2x+4} \\ & \phantom{2x^2 - x - 2} \:\:\:\:\: \phantom{4x^4-2x^3-4x^2+} \:\: \phantom{0}x - 3 \end{align*}

Therefore,

  • the quotient is $2x^2 - 2,$ and

  • the remainder is ${x -3}.$

Therefore, \[ \dfrac{4x^4-2x^3-8x^2+3x+1}{2x^2-x-2}=2x^2-2 + \dfrac{x-3}{2x^2-x-2}. \]

question.text: What is the remainder when $-12x^4+28x^3-47x^2+25x-9$ is divided by $6x^2 - 5x + 4?$
question.explanation:
Using the method of polynomial division, we obtain the following:

\begin{align*} \require{enclose} & \phantom{6x^2 - 5x + 4} \:\:\:\:\: -2x^2 + 3x - 4 \\ & 6x^2 - 5x + 4 \: \enclose{longdiv}{\:\, -12x^4+28x^3-47x^2+25x-\phantom{0}9 \:\:} \\ & \phantom{6x^2 - 5x + 4} \:\:\:\:\: \underline{-12x^4+10x^3-8x^2} \\ & \phantom{6x^2 - 5x + 4} \:\:\:\:\:\:\: \phantom{-12x^4+} 18x^3-39x^2+25x-\phantom{0}9 \\ & \phantom{6x^2 - 5x + 4} \:\:\:\:\:\:\: \phantom{-12x^4+} \underline{18x^3-15x^2+12x} \\ & \phantom{6x^2 - 5x + 4} \:\:\:\:\: \phantom{-12x^4+18x^3} -24x^2 +13x - \phantom{0}9 \\ & \phantom{6x^2 - 5x + 4} \:\:\:\:\:\: \phantom{-12x^4+18x^3} \underline{-\:24x^2+20x-16 } \\ & \phantom{6x^2 - 5x + 4} \:\:\:\:\:\: \phantom{-12x^4+18x^3-24x^2 +} {\color{blue}-7x +\phantom{0}7} \\ \end{align*}

Therefore,

  • the quotient is $-2x^2 + 3x - 4,$ and

  • the remainder is ${\color{blue}-7x +7}.$

exampleAnswers.title: Dividing Polynomials When the Dividend Contains Zero Coefficients

question.text: What is the remainder when $-2x^4+x^3-3x^2+1$ is divided by $2x^2-x+5?$
question.explanation:
Notice that the dividend is missing the $x$ term. So, we first rewrite it by including the missing term with a coefficient of zero, as follows:

\[ -2x^4+x^3-3x^2+1 = -2x^4+x^3-3x^2+{\color{red}0}x+1 \]

Now, using the method of polynomial division, we obtain the following:

\begin{align*} \require{enclose} & \phantom{2x^2-x+5} \:\:\:\: -x^2 + 1 \\ & 2x^2-x+5 \: \enclose{longdiv}{\:\, -2x^4+x^3-3x^2+0x+1 \:\:} \\ & \phantom{2x^2-x+5} \:\:\:\: \underline{-\,2x^4+x^3-5x^2} \\ & \phantom{2x^2-x+5} \:\:\:\:\: \phantom{-\,2x^4+x^3-} 2x^2+0x+1 \\ & \phantom{2x^2-x+5} \:\:\:\:\: \phantom{-\,2x^4+x^3-} \underline{2x^2-\phantom{0}x+5} \\ & \phantom{2x^2-x+5} \:\:\:\:\: \phantom{-\,2x^4+x^3-3x^2+} {\color{blue}\phantom{0}x-4} \\ \end{align*}

Therefore,

  • the quotient is $-x^2 + 1,$ and

  • the remainder is ${\color{blue}x-4}.$

question.text: What is the quotient of $8x^4+24x+2$ divided by $-2x^2 + 3x - 5?$
question.explanation:
Notice that the dividend is missing the $x^3$ and $x^2$ terms. So, we first rewrite it by including the missing terms with zero coefficients, as follows:

\[ 8x^4+24x+2 = 8x^4+{\color{red}0}x^3+{\color{red}0}x^2+24x+2 \]

Now, using the method of polynomial division, we obtain the following:

\begin{align*} \require{enclose} & \phantom{-2x^2 + 3x - 5} \:\:\:\:\: {\color{blue}-4x^2-6x+1} \\ & {-2x^2 + 3x - 5} \: \enclose{longdiv}{\:\, 8x^4+\phantom{0}0x^3+\phantom{0}0x^2+24x+2 \:\:} \\ & \phantom{-2x^2 + 3x - 5} \:\:\:\:\: \underline{8x^4-12x^3+20x^2} \\ & \phantom{-2x^2 + 3x - 5} \:\:\:\:\:\:\: \phantom{8x^4+} 12x^3-20x^2+24x+2 \\ & \phantom{-2x^2 + 3x - 5} \:\:\:\:\:\:\: \phantom{8x^4+} \underline{12x^3-18x^2+30x} \\ & \phantom{-2x^2 + 3x - 5} \:\:\:\:\:\: \phantom{8x^4+12x^3} {-\: \phantom{0}2x^2-\phantom{0}6x+2} \\ & \phantom{-2x^2 + 3x - 5} \:\:\:\:\:\: \phantom{8x^4+12x^3} \underline{-\: \phantom{0}2x^2+\phantom{0}3x-5} \\ & \phantom{-2x^2 + 3x - 5} \:\:\:\:\:\: \phantom{8x^4+12x^3-\phantom{0}2x^2} {-\: \phantom{0}9x+7} \end{align*}

Therefore,

  • the quotient is $\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{-4x^2-6x+1},$ and

  • the remainder is ${-9x+7}.$

question.text: What is the quotient of $12x^4-5$ divided by $-2x^2 + 2x - 3?$
question.explanation:
Notice that the dividend is missing the $x^3, x^2$ and $x$ terms. So, we first rewrite it by including the missing terms with zero coefficients, as follows:

\[ 12x^4-5 = 12x^4+{\color{red}0}x^3+{\color{red}0}x^2+{\color{red}0}x-5 \]

Now, using the method of polynomial division, we obtain the following:

\begin{align*} \require{enclose} & \phantom{-2x^2 + 2x - 3} \:\:\:\:\: {\color{blue}-6x^2-6x+3} \\ & {-2x^2 + 2x - 3} \: \enclose{longdiv}{\:\, 12x^4+\phantom{0}0x^3+\phantom{0}0x^2+\phantom{0}0x-5 \:\:} \\ & \phantom{-2x^2 + 2x - 3} \:\:\:\:\: \underline{12x^4-12x^3+18x^2} \\ & \phantom{-2x^2 + 2x - 3} \:\:\:\:\:\:\: \phantom{12x^4+} 12x^3-18x^2+\phantom{0}0x-5 \\ & \phantom{-2x^2 + 2x - 3} \:\:\:\:\:\:\: \phantom{12x^4+} \underline{12x^3-12x^2+18x} \\ & \phantom{-2x^2 + 2x - 3} \:\:\:\:\:\: \phantom{12x^4+12x^3} {-\: \phantom{0}6x^2-18x-5} \\ & \phantom{-2x^2 + 2x - 3} \:\:\:\:\:\: \phantom{12x^4+12x^3} \underline{-\: \phantom{0}6x^2+\phantom{0}6x-9} \\ & \phantom{-2x^2 + 2x - 3} \:\:\:\:\:\: \phantom{12x^4+12x^3-\phantom{0}6x^2} {-\: 24x+4} \end{align*}

Therefore,

  • the quotient is $\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{-6x^2-6x+3},$ and

  • the remainder is ${-24x+4}.$

example.title: Dividing Polynomials When the Dividend Contains Zero Coefficients

question.explanation:
Notice that the dividend is missing the $x^3$ term. So, we first rewrite it by including the missing term with a coefficient of zero, as follows:

\[ 2x^4-11x^2+2x+1 = 2x^4+{\color{red}0}x^3-11x^2+2x+1 \]

Now, using the method of polynomial division, we obtain the following:

\begin{align*} \require{enclose} & \phantom{-2x^3+6x^2-1} \:\:\:\: -x - 3 \\ & -2x^3+6x^2-1 \: \enclose{longdiv}{\:\, 2x^4+0x^3-11x^2+2x+1 \:\:} \\ & \phantom{-2x^3+6x^2-1} \:\:\:\:\:\:\: \underline{2x^4-6x^3+\phantom{0}0x^2+\phantom{0}x} \\ & \phantom{-2x^3+6x^2-1} \:\:\:\:\:\:\:\:\: \phantom{2x^4+} 6x^3-11x^2+\phantom{0}x+1 \\ & \phantom{-2x^3+6x^2-1} \:\:\:\:\:\:\:\:\: \phantom{2x^4+} \underline{6x^3-18x^2+0x+3} \\ & \phantom{-2x^3+6x^2-1} \:\:\:\:\:\:\:\:\: \phantom{2x^4+6x^3+} {\phantom{0}7x^2+\phantom{0}x-2} \\ \end{align*}

As a result,

  • the quotient is $-x - 3,$ and

  • the remainder is ${7x^2+x-2}.$

Therefore, \[ \dfrac{2x^4 - 11x^2 + 2x + 1}{-2x^3+6x^2-1}=-x-3 + \dfrac{7x^2+x-2}{-2x^3+6x^2-1}. \]
